# wiresizes.com

> Wire gauge charts, NEC table values and calculators for sizing conductors.

## Calculators

- [Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/wire-size-calculator): Copper or aluminum conductor size for a breaker or fuse rating from 15 to 400 A, from NEC Table 310.16 (2023) in the column the terminals allow under 110.14(C) (NM and UF cable at 60 °C), corrected for ambient temperature and more than three current-carrying conductors and limited by 240.4(D), with the 125 % continuous-load check of 210.20(A); equipment grounding conductor from Table 250.122, not larger than the conductors (250.122(A)) and grown in proportion when the drop moves them up (250.122(B)); voltage drop at the load current over a one-way length, stepping to larger sizes until it meets the target you choose; a note where 240.4(B) lets the rating protect the next smaller size.
- [Voltage Drop Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/voltage-drop-calculator): Voltage drop in volts and percent, and the power lost in the conductors, for a Table 310.16 conductor size, current, one-way length and voltage, single- or three-phase, with solid-conductor DC resistance at 75 °C calculated from NIST Handbook 100 and 109.
- [Ampacity Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ampacity-calculator): Table 310.16 (2023) ampacity for a size, material and insulation temperature column, multiplied by the ambient correction factor from Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) and the adjustment for more than three current-carrying conductors from Table 310.15(C)(1), shown against the 60 °C and 75 °C terminal limits of 110.14(C) and the 240.4(D) breaker limit.
- [Circuit Breaker Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/circuit-breaker-calculator): Breaker or fuse rating for a continuous and a noncontinuous load: at least the noncontinuous load plus 125 % of the continuous load (NEC 210.20(A)), rounded up to a standard rating of Table 240.6(A) from 15 to 400 A; the wire for that rating in the column the terminals allow, the 240.4(D) limits, the Table 250.122 ground wire and the next smaller wire 240.4(B) allows; the largest breaker for each wire size.
- [Ground Wire Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ground-wire-calculator): Equipment grounding conductor size in copper and in aluminum or copper-clad aluminum for an overcurrent device rated 15 A to 6000 A, from NEC Table 250.122 (2023); with the circuit wires entered, it grows in proportion to upsized wires (250.122(B)) and is not larger than them (250.122(A)).
- [Wire Resistance Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/wire-resistance-calculator): Resistance of one conductor and of the circuit loop at a conductor temperature, from the 20 °C values of NIST Handbook 100 (copper) and Handbook 109 (aluminum EC-H19) and their temperature coefficients, and the power lost at a given current.
- [Service Entrance Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/service-entrance-calculator): Copper and aluminum conductor sizes from NEC Table 310.12 (2023) for a 120/240 V single-phase service, or a feeder, that carries the entire load of a one-family dwelling or of one dwelling unit, rated 100 to 400 A; the grounding electrode conductor for each from Table 250.66; and the voltage drop over a length you enter.
- [Garage Subpanel Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/garage-subpanel-calculator): the feeder to a subpanel in a detached garage for a 30 to 200 A breaker: copper or aluminum conductors from NEC Table 310.16 at the terminal temperature (110.14(C)), the ground wire from Table 250.122, four wires (250.32), a garage disconnect of at least 60 A (225.39), the voltage drop and the minimum cover of Table 300.5(A) (2023).
- [Residential Load Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/residential-load-calculator): A dwelling unit's calculated load by both methods of NEC 2023 Article 220 on the same inputs, every step shown. Standard method: 3 VA per ft² and 1,500 VA per small-appliance and laundry circuit through Table 220.45, 75 % for four or more appliances fastened in place (220.53), the dryer at 5,000 W or its nameplate (220.54), one range from Table 220.55, an EV charger at 7,200 W or its nameplate (220.57), and the larger of the heating at 100 % and the cooling at 125 % (220.51, 220.60). Optional method (220.82): the first 10 kVA of the general load at 100 % and the rest at 40 %, plus the largest heating or cooling selection. Each total divided by 240 V, with the smallest Table 310.12 service at or above it.
- [Range Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/range-calculator): The branch-circuit load of household cooking appliances by NEC 2023 Table 220.55: one range from Column C (8 kW up to 12 kW) with Note 1 above (5 % per kW, up to 27 kW); one wall-mounted oven or counter-mounted cooking unit at its nameplate; a cooktop with up to two wall ovens on one circuit in one room added and treated as one range. The current at 240 or 208 V, and the wire (Table 310.16 in the terminal column, 240.4(D)) and ground wire (Table 250.122) for the circuit rating the range instructions give; Whirlpool's and Frigidaire's stated circuits and cords; NEMA 14-50R and 10-50R; 210.8(D) GFCI.
- [Dryer Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/dryer-calculator): An electric clothes dryer's two numbers kept apart: its load on a feeder or service under NEC 2023 220.54 (5,000 W or the nameplate, whichever is larger) with Table 220.54's demand factors for several dryers, and the wire and ground wire for its own circuit at the rating its instructions give (Whirlpool and GE: 30 A, 10 AWG copper). NEMA 14-30R and 10-30R; the 2023 210.8(D) GFCI rule.
- [Low Voltage Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/low-voltage-calculator): Copper conductor size for a DC load from the circular mils its voltage-drop target needs (CM = 2 × K × I × L ÷ VD, K from NIST Handbook 100 at 20 °C or 75 °C) and from its current in the 60 °C column of NEC Table 310.16; the larger size applies.
- [RV Hookup Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/rv-hookup-calculator): The circuit for a TT-30R (30 A, 125 V) or 14-50R (50 A, 125/250 V) RV outlet from NEC Table 310.16 at the terminal temperature with the Table 250.122 ground wire and the voltage drop over the run; GFCI by 210.8(F) at a house and 551.71(F) at a park; and an RV park feeder from 551.73(A) (12,000 VA per 50 A site, 3600 VA per 20 A and 30 A site, 2400 VA per 20 A site) and the Table 551.73(A) demand factors (100 % for one site down to 41 % for 36 or more).
- [Well Pump Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/well-pump-calculator): The copper cable size for a Franklin Electric 4-inch single-phase submersible motor (115 V 1/2 hp; 230 V 1/2 to 5 hp, 2-wire to 1.5 hp) from the total cable length, using Franklin's 2026 AIM Manual table at a 5 % drop (or 3 %, the length times 0.6), shaded cells skipped for jacketed cable, aluminum two sizes larger; with Franklin's breaker and fuse sizes (the NEC maximum and the typical size) and the motor's line amps.
- [Hot Tub Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/hot-tub-calculator): The copper circuit for the breaker a hot tub's manual asks for (30 to 60 A at 240 V, 15 or 20 A at 120 V) from NEC Table 310.16 at the terminal temperature, with the Table 250.122 ground wire and the voltage drop over the run; four wires at 240 V; and what Hot Spring, Bullfrog and Marquis require in their 2026 manuals: a 50 A circuit (Bullfrog also 60 A), GFCI protection, copper only, Marquis's three 6 AWG and 8 AWG ground, the disconnect within sight and at least 5 ft from the hot tub.
- [Air Conditioner Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/air-conditioner-calculator): The copper circuit for an air conditioner from the two numbers on its nameplate (NEC 440.4(B)): the wire sized to the minimum circuit ampacity (MCA) in NEC Table 310.16 at the terminal temperature; a breaker or fuse up to the nameplate's maximum (MOCP), which Table 240.4(G) and Article 440 allow above the 240.4(D) limits; the Table 250.122 ground wire, not larger than the circuit conductors (250.122(A)); and the voltage drop at the MCA over the run. With the MCA and MOCP of Carrier's 26SCA5 and Amana's ALXS3N 1.5- to 5-ton units from their 2025 product data, both of which ask for copper wire.
- [Welder Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/welder-calculator): The copper circuit for a 240 V welder from its manual: the wire from the manual's minimum, moved up until NEC 630.12(B) allows the breaker (at most 200 % of the wire's ampacity) and then for the voltage drop at I1max over the run; the breaker at most 200 % of I1max (630.12(A)), the next standard rating permitted, with Table 240.4(G) lifting the 240.4(D) caps; the Table 250.122 ground wire. With the electrical service guides of six Miller and Lincoln welders, 630.13's disconnect and 630.8's GFCI rule for the welding area. The NEC's own rule for sizing welder supply conductors is not stated.
- [Box Fill Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/box-fill-calculator): Whether an electrical box is large enough under NEC 2023 314.16: each conductor at its Table 314.16(B)(1) volume (2.00 in³ at 14 AWG, 2.25 in³ at 12 AWG), two allowances per device yoke, one for up to four ground wires and a quarter for each more, one for internal clamps and one per type of support fitting, against the volume of a Table 314.16(A) metal box or the volume marked on the box.
- [Three Phase Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/three-phase-calculator): Balanced three-phase conversion between power and line current at a line-to-line voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF).
- [Watts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/watts-to-amps-calculator): Current from power, voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (V × PF) single-phase and I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF) three-phase.
- [Amps to Watts](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/amps-to-watts-calculator): Real power, apparent power and electrical horsepower (746 W) from current, voltage and power factor.
- [Volts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/volts-to-amps-calculator): Current from power, voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (V × PF) single-phase and I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF) three-phase.
- [Kilowatts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/kilowatts-to-amps-calculator): Current, apparent power and reactive power from kilowatts, voltage and power factor, single- or three-phase.
- [kVA to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/kva-to-amps-calculator): Current from apparent power and voltage, single- or three-phase.
- [Horsepower to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/horsepower-to-amps-calculator): A motor's full-load current from NEC 2023 Tables 430.248 (single-phase), 430.250 (three-phase induction) and 430.247 (DC) by horsepower and the voltage column the tables' notes give, never from a formula (430.6(A)): a 1 hp single-phase motor is 16 A at 115 V and 8 A at 230 V. Also the rating in watts (746 W per horsepower, NIST SP 811). No wire or breaker sizing for motor circuits.
- [BTU to Watts](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/btu-to-watts-calculator): Btu per hour to watts and tons of refrigeration and back, with 1 Btu/h = 0.2930711 W (NIST SP 811) and 1 ton = 12,000 Btu/h.
- [Ohm's Law Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ohms-law-calculator): Voltage, current, resistance and power from any two of them, V = I × R and P = V × I.

## Charts and guides

- [AWG Wire Size Chart](https://wiresizes.com/guides/awg-wire-size-chart): AWG sizes with diameter, cross-sectional area and solid annealed copper resistance at 20 °C from NIST Handbook 100, and copper and aluminum ampacities from NEC Table 310.16 (2023).
- [NEC Table 310.16](https://wiresizes.com/guides/nec-table-310-16): All 30 rows of NEC Table 310.16 (2023), copper and aluminum in the 60, 75 and 90 °C columns, with the 16 ambient correction rows of Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) and the adjustment factors of Table 310.15(C)(1).
- [Wire Size for 200 Amp](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-200-amp): 2/0 AWG copper or 4/0 AWG aluminum for a 120/240 V dwelling service, from NEC Table 310.12 (2023).
- [Wire Size for 100 Amp Subpanel or Service](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-100-amp): 1 AWG copper or 1/0 AWG aluminum for a 100 A subpanel feeder at 60 °C terminals (3 AWG or 1 AWG where every termination is listed for 75 °C), 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum for a 120/240 V dwelling service, and the four-wire feeder to a detached garage, from NEC Tables 310.16 and 310.12, 225.39 and 250.32 (2023).
- [Wire Size for EV Charger](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-ev-charger): the breaker and copper wire for 16 to 48 A Level 2 chargers, from 12 AWG on a 20 A breaker to 6 AWG at 75 °C terminals or 4 AWG NM cable on a 60 A breaker for 48 A, from NEC 625.41, 625.42 and Table 310.16 (2023) and the Tesla, ChargePoint and Emporia instructions; the plug-in and GFCI rules of 625.44 and 625.54, the ground wire and the voltage drop.
- [Electrical Power Calculations](https://wiresizes.com/guides/electrical-power-calculations): Formulas for power, current, voltage and resistance in DC, single-phase and three-phase circuits.
- [Single vs Three Phase](https://wiresizes.com/guides/single-vs-three-phase): Single-phase and three-phase voltage systems and the power formulas for each.
- [Power Factor Explained](https://wiresizes.com/guides/power-factor-explained): Real, reactive and apparent power and power factor, PF = P ÷ S.
- [NEC Edition by State](https://wiresizes.com/guides/nec-code-compliance): the National Electrical Code edition each state and DC has adopted, with its start date, scope and any scheduled change, each row linked to the state's record; the 2026 edition's dates and the changes Minnesota's review of it lists.

## Site

- [Home](https://wiresizes.com/): Calculator and guide links; copper sizes for 15 to 40 A circuits from the 60 °C column of NEC Table 310.16 (2023); dwelling service sizes from Table 310.12; grounding electrode conductors from Table 250.66.
- [Calculators](https://wiresizes.com/calculators): List of the calculators.
- [Guides](https://wiresizes.com/guides): List of the guides.
- [About](https://wiresizes.com/about): Who writes wiresizes.com, which sources its numbers come from, how pages are checked, and the dated list of corrections.
- [Methodology](https://wiresizes.com/methodology): The sources behind the calculators, with the edition of each, the formulas used, their limits, and the topics not covered yet.
- [Contact](https://wiresizes.com/contact): Email address for corrections, questions about a page and privacy requests.
- [Privacy notice](https://wiresizes.com/privacy): What wiresizes.com collects, which services process it, the legal basis, and how to use your data protection rights.
- [Terms of use](https://wiresizes.com/terms): Who operates wiresizes.com, what its tables and calculators are for, and what they don't cover.
- [Disclaimer](https://wiresizes.com/disclaimer): The limits of the tables and calculators on wiresizes.com, and who has the final word on an installation.
